title: Compatible roots of unity and the prime-to-p product of adic integers
statement:
Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-algebraic-closure] of characteristic $p>0$. For a positive integer $m$ prime to $p$, put $\mu_m(k)=\{z\in k^\times:z^m=1\}$, with its discrete topology. There exists a family of primitive roots $\zeta_m\in\mu_m(k)$ (each $\zeta_m$ has multiplicative order exactly $m$) for all such $m$ with $\zeta_1=1$ and $\zeta_n^{n/m}=\zeta_m$ whenever $m\mid n$. For any such family, the maps $\mathbf Z/m\mathbf Z\to\mu_m(k)$, $a\mapsto\zeta_m^a$, induce an isomorphism of topological groups
$$
\varprojlim_{(m,p)=1}\mu_m(k)\cong\prod_{r\text{ prime},\ r\ne p}(\mathbf Z_r,+),
$$
where the transition from $\mu_n(k)$ to $\mu_m(k)$ is $z\mapsto z^{n/m}$, the inverse limit and product have their standard inverse-limit and product topologies, and $\mathbf Z_r$ is the ring of adic integers [def-weil-l-adic-numbers], identified topologically with $\varprojlim_{a\ge1}\mathbf Z/r^a\mathbf Z$. The isomorphism is allowed to depend on the family of primitive roots.

source.place: Tag 09HW (section-roots-of-1: finite cyclic root groups); algebra.tex Tag 00DT (lemma-chinese-remainder); the inverse-limit construction used at pione.tex Tag 0BUB (lemma-structure-decomposition-separable-closure). This statement packages the compatible-generator and Chinese-remainder consequences, not a verbatim assertion of 0BUB.

proof.text: First prove that every primitive root of order $n$ lifts to a primitive root of order $N$ under the power map whenever $n\mid N$ and both are prime to $p$. By [lem-sc-primitive-root], choose a primitive $N$-th root $\eta$. The element $\eta^{N/n}$ has order $n$: its $d$-th power is $1$ exactly when $N\mid (N/n)d$, or $n\mid d$. It generates $\mu_n(k)$, so the prescribed primitive root is $(\eta^{N/n})^b$ with $b$ prime to $n$. Use [lem-pc-crt-ideal-quotient-product] over $\mathbf Z$ to choose a nonnegative integer $a$ with $a\equiv b\pmod n$ and $a\equiv1\pmod q$ for every prime $q\mid N$ not dividing $n$. These ideals are pairwise coprime by Bezout's identity. Every prime dividing $N$ either divides $n$, and hence cannot divide $a$, or occurs among these $q$, and again cannot divide $a$. Thus $a$ is prime to $N$. The root $\eta^a$ has order $N$ (if $N\mid ad$, Bezout gives $N\mid d$), and $(\eta^a)^{N/n}$ is the prescribed root. For $n=1$ the congruence modulo $1$ imposes no condition; for $N=1$ take $\eta=1$.

source.place: Tag 09HW (section-roots-of-1), finite cyclic groups; algebra.tex Tag 00DT (lemma-chinese-remainder), applied to the displayed integer ideals

proof.text: Put $N_0=1$ and $N_j=\prod_{1\leq i\leq j,\ (i,p)=1}i$. Each $N_j$ is positive and prime to $p$, $N_j\mid N_{j+1}$, and every positive $m$ prime to $p$ divides $N_j$ for all $j\geq m$. Starting with $\eta_0=1$, use Step 1 recursively to choose a primitive $N_{j+1}$-th root $\eta_{j+1}$ such that $\eta_{j+1}^{N_{j+1}/N_j}=\eta_j$. Composing these equations gives $\eta_b^{N_b/N_a}=\eta_a$ for $a\leq b$. Repeated values of $N_j$ force equal roots because the exponent is $1$.

source.place: Tag 09HW (section-roots-of-1); explicit recursive choice using Step 1

proof.text: For $m$ prime to $p$, choose any $j\geq m$ and set $\zeta_m=\eta_j^{N_j/m}$. If $j'$ is another choice, compare both with an index $b\geq j,j'$ and use $\eta_b^{N_b/N_j}=\eta_j$; both expressions equal $\eta_b^{N_b/m}$. This proves independence. Since $\eta_j$ has order $N_j$, the equation $(\eta_j^{N_j/m})^d=1$ is equivalent to $m\mid d$, so $\zeta_m$ has order $m$. For $m\mid n$ take a single $j\geq n$ and compute $\zeta_n^{n/m}=\eta_j^{(N_j/n)(n/m)}=\zeta_m$; in particular $\zeta_1=1$.

source.place: Tag 09HW (section-roots-of-1); explicit all-orders compatibility constructed from the cofinal sequence

proof.text: Now let $(\zeta_m)_m$ be any family satisfying the statement, including one just constructed. By [lem-sc-primitive-root], $\mu_m(k)$ has $m$ elements. The map $\theta_m:\mathbf Z/m\mathbf Z\to\mu_m(k)$, $[a]\mapsto\zeta_m^a$, is a homomorphism and is injective by the order-$m$ condition, hence bijective. For $m\mid n$ its transition satisfies $(\zeta_n^a)^{n/m}=\zeta_m^a$, exactly reduction of $[a]$ modulo $m$. Consequently $(a_m)_m\mapsto(\theta_m(a_m))_m$ gives an isomorphism from $C=\varprojlim_{(m,p)=1}\mathbf Z/m\mathbf Z$ to the root limit; its inverse applies $\theta_m^{-1}$ in each coordinate. All levels are discrete, and the preimage of a coordinate cylinder is a coordinate cylinder, in both directions. Thus this is an isomorphism of topological groups.

source.place: Tag 09HW (section-roots-of-1); compatibility of the finite cyclic identifications and the inverse-limit topology

proof.text: For $m=\prod_{r\mid m}r^{v_r(m)}$, apply [lem-pc-crt-ideal-quotient-product] to the finitely many ideals $r^{v_r(m)}\mathbf Z$ in $\mathbf Z$. Distinct prime powers are coprime by Bezout. Their intersection is $m\mathbf Z$, since an integer is divisible by all these prime powers exactly when it is divisible by their product. This gives the ring isomorphism $\gamma_m:\mathbf Z/m\mathbf Z\to\prod_{r\mid m}\mathbf Z/r^{v_r(m)}\mathbf Z$ by ordinary reductions. If $m=1$, the index set is empty and both sides are the one-element ring. If $m\mid n$, reducing a residue modulo $n$ first modulo $m$ and then modulo $r^{v_r(m)}$ is the same as reducing it directly to that prime power; this follows by taking an integer representative.

source.place: Tag 00DT (lemma-chinese-remainder), finite prime-power ideals in the integers

proof.text: For a prime $r\ne p$, let $R_r$ be the ring of compatible sequences $b_{r,a}\in\mathbf Z/r^a\mathbf Z$, $a\geq1$, with its subspace topology in the product of the discrete quotient rings. Restriction defines $C\to\prod_{r\ne p}R_r$ by $(a_m)_m\mapsto((a_{r^a})_{a\geq1})_r$. Conversely, given $(b_{r,a})$, let $a_m$ be the unique residue whose reductions are $b_{r,v_r(m)}$ for $r\mid m$, using $\gamma_m$ of Step 5. For $m\mid n$, compatibility of each $b_{r,a}$ shows that $a_n\bmod m$ and $a_m$ have identical reductions at every prime power dividing $m$, so injectivity of $\gamma_m$ makes them equal. Taking $m=r^a$ recovers $b_{r,a}$; applying $\gamma_m$ recovers every original $a_m$. These are inverse ring maps. Restriction is continuous since its coordinates are input projections. Each output $a_m$ of the inverse depends on the finitely many discrete coordinates $b_{r,v_r(m)}$, so its fibres are open cylinders. This proves continuity of the inverse and hence the asserted topological product decomposition of $C$.

source.place: Tag 00DT (lemma-chinese-remainder); the explicit restriction and reconstruction of compatible residue coordinates

proof.text: Fix $r\ne p$. Append the unique coordinate modulo $r^0=1$ to $R_r$. Coordinatewise addition and multiplication preserve compatibility, so this is a commutative unital ring and each projection $f_a:R_r\to\mathbf Z/r^a\mathbf Z$ is a unital ring homomorphism. Apply [lem-exc-padic-residue-universal-property] with this source ring and these compatible projections to obtain $\psi_r:R_r\to\mathbf Z_r$ with $\rho_a\psi_r=f_a$. The same node says that the residues $\rho_a$ are compatible, so they define $\phi_r:\mathbf Z_r\to R_r$. The equality $\phi_r\psi_r=1$ follows at every coordinate from $\rho_a\psi_r=f_a$. For $x\in\mathbf Z_r$, $\psi_r\phi_r(x)$ and $x$ have equal residues at every level; point separation in that node proves $\psi_r\phi_r(x)=x$. Thus these are inverse ring isomorphisms. Appending or deleting the unique zero-th coordinate changes neither the ring nor its topology.

source.place: Tag 00M9 (section-completion), compatible sequences; exact specialization of the Mathlib residue universal property recorded in the cited leaf

proof.text: The same residue lemma gives $\ker\rho_a=r^a\mathbf Z_r$ and $r^a\mathbf Z_r=\{x:|x|_r\leq r^{-a}\}$. The open norm ball $\{y\in\mathbf Z_r:|y-x|_r<r^{-a}\}$ about $x$ is contained in the fibre of $\rho_a(x)$, since $|y-x|_r<r^{-a}$ implies $y-x\in r^a\mathbf Z_r$ by the displayed equality. This open neighbourhood at each $x$ proves that every residue map to its discrete quotient is locally constant. It follows by inverse images of coordinate cylinders that $\phi_r$ is continuous. Conversely, given $b\in R_r$ and $\epsilon>0$, choose $a\geq1$ with $r^{-a}<\epsilon$ (since $r>1$). If $b'$ agrees with $b$ at coordinate $a$, then $\rho_a(\psi_r(b')-\psi_r(b))=0$ and the displayed kernel/norm equality gives $|\psi_r(b')-\psi_r(b)|_r\leq r^{-a}<\epsilon$. The coordinate-$a$ cylinder is an open neighbourhood of $b$, which proves continuity of $\psi_r$. Thus $R_r\cong\mathbf Z_r$ topologically. This argument uses the norm and topology of the valuation-ring definition, rather than assuming that definition already is an inverse limit.

source.place: Tag 00M9 (section-completion), residue topology; norm and kernel clauses of the cited Mathlib leaf

proof.text: Take the product of the mutually inverse continuous maps $\phi_r,\psi_r$; continuity follows coordinatewise in the product topology. Compose the inverse of the root/residue isomorphism in Step 4 with the isomorphism of Step 6 and these product isomorphisms. This gives exactly $\varprojlim_{(m,p)=1}\mu_m(k)\cong\prod_{r\ne p}(\mathbf Z_r,+)$. The finite maps used in Step 4 are precisely $[a]\mapsto\zeta_m^a$, so the resulting isomorphism is the one induced by the chosen family as required. Only that choice is noncanonical; Steps 5--8 use the canonical residue maps.
